facts.text: The stubble quail is a plump ground-dwelling bird with dark brown feathers, each marked with a cream stripe that runs down the length of the bird.
facts.quote: The stubble quail is a ground dwelling bird that is characterised by its dark brown feathers with a cream coloured strip down the centre of each feather giving rise to stripes down the length of the bird.

facts.text: When a stubble quail is startled into flight, its wings make a loud whirring noise.
facts.quote: The stubble quail can also be identified by the loud whirring noise made by their wings during take-off into flight once disturbed from on the ground.

facts.text: Males call at dawn and dusk as a territorial display.
facts.quote: Males call at dawn and dusk as a territorial display.

facts.text: The female lays about seven or eight yellow eggs and incubates them alone for 18 days.
facts.quote: The female stubble quail lays about seven or eight yellow eggs which are incubated solely by her for 18 days.

facts.text: Stubble quail often nest in crops that are about to be harvested, so their nests are frequently destroyed.
facts.quote: Often stubble quail nest in crops that are about to be harvested so their nests get destroyed.

facts.text: Stubble quail are nomadic and can travel very long distances, with the furthest recorded journey at 1142 km.
facts.quote: Stubble quail are nomadic and move to available resources; however, when resources are very limited, they tend to scatter in all directions. They can travel very long distances with the furthest recorded at 1142 km.

facts.text: With access to green foliage as well as grain, the stubble quail can survive without drinking any water.
facts.quote: If the birds have access to green foliage as well as grain, the stubble quail can survive without drinking any water.

facts.text: In very hot areas, stubble quail forage during the night to escape the heat.
facts.quote: In areas where temperatures are very hot, stubble quail have been observed to forage during the night.

facts.text: Stubble quail avoid wooded areas and prefer tall, dense grasslands made up of native or introduced grasses and crops.
facts.quote: On the mainland stubble quail are found in a variety of biomes but tend to avoid wooded areas as the canopy obstructs the growth of thick grassy undergrowth that they prefer. They prefer a habitat of tall grassland made up of native or introduced grasses, and crops.

facts.text: It is the only native upland game bird that can be legally hunted in Australia, under strict game law restrictions.
facts.quote: It is the only native upland game bird that can be legally hunted in Australia, though with strict game law restrictions.
